tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q3 fiscal 2025

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue Q3 fiscal 2025

NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue was **$30.8 billion** in **Q3 fiscal 2025** (quarter ended October 27, 2024), increasing **17% quarter over quarter** and **112% year over year**. [[1]]

Related coverage:
**Revenue.** NVIDIA reported record Automotive revenue of **$2.349 billion in FY2026** (year ended January 25, 2026), versus **$1.694 billion in FY2025** and **$1.091 billion in FY2024**—a **39% year-over-year increase** driven by adoption of its self-driving platforms. [[1, 2]] 
The business generated **$604 million in Q4 FY2026**, up **2% sequentially** and **6% year over year**. [[3]] 
Automotive was nevertheless only about **1.1%** of NVIDIA’s **$215.938 billion** FY2026 consolidated revenue, so it remains a strategically important but financially small vertical relative to Data Center. [[1]] 
Management had forecast the automotive vertical could reach approximately **$5 billion in FY2026** in January 2025; actual FY2026 revenue of $2.349 billion was therefore about **47% of that earlier estimate**. [[4, 1]]

**What NVIDIA sells into autonomy.** NVIDIA’s proposition is an end-to-end DRIVE stack: accelerated AI infrastructure for training, simulation tooling, in-vehicle DRIVE AGX compute, DriveOS, sensor/reference architecture through DRIVE Hyperion, and safety software through Halos OS. [[4, 5]] 
The company’s revised reporting from Q1 FY2027 no longer separately discloses an A

events.content:
**Summary of NVIDIA Data Center revenue findings (most recent fiscal quarters):**

| Quarter (Fiscal Year) | Data Center Revenue | YoY Growth | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 FY2025 (ended Jan 26 2025) | **$35.6 B** | **+93%** | S1.1 |
| Q3 FY2025 (ended Oct 27 2024) | **$30.8 B** | **+112%** | S3.1 |
| Q2 FY2025 (ended Apr 28 2024) | **$26.3 B** | **+154%** | S5.1 |
| Q1 FY2025 (ended Jul 30 2023) | **$26.3 B** (per S7.1, reported with Q2) | +154% YoY | S7.1 |

**Key growth drivers cited in the filings:**
- Massive demand for AI training and inference GPUs (e.g., Hopper, Ada Lovelace architectures) from cloud providers and enterprise customers.
- Expansion of generative AI workloads, large language model training, and increasing adoption of NVIDIA‑DGX and HGX platforms.
- Growth in enterprise software and networking (e.g., Spectrum-X, NVLink) that complements the GPU installations.
- Seasonal and sequential quarter‑over‑quarter increases driven by large‑scale customer purchase cadence and new product ramps.

All figures are sourced directly from NVIDIA’s official earnings releases and SEC filings.
